quality_snapshot.text:
Rain drummed softly against the window, each patter a reminder of the world outside, where the streets gleamed under a slick sheen of water, reflecting the blurred halo of streetlights. Inside, the warmth of the small café enveloped Clara like a well-worn blanket. The scent of freshly ground coffee beans mingled with the sweet aroma of pastries, creating an intoxicating atmosphere that made her relax for the first time that day. She curled her fingers around the warm ceramic mug, feeling the heat seep into her skin, grounding her in the moment.

Across the table, Tom stirred his espresso, his brow furrowed in thought. The faint clink of the spoon against the cup punctuated the silence between them. Clara watched him, trying to decipher the storm brewing behind his dark eyes, those eyes that had once sparkled with laughter, now clouded with something unspoken. She opened her mouth, the words hovering on the tip of her tongue, but hesitated, unsure if she wanted to provoke whatever tidal wave of emotion was simmering beneath the surface.

“Do you remember the last time we were here?” His voice was low, almost drowned out by the soft chatter of other patrons and the hiss of the espresso machine. He didn’t look up, concentrating instead on the swirling liquid in his cup.

“Of course,” she said, her heart tightening at the memory. It was a day much like this, the rain falling gently, laughter spilling between them like the coffee they had shared. “You spilled your drink all over that poor waitress.”

He finally lifted his gaze, a ghost of a smile flickering across his lips. “I was young and reckless.”

“Reckless? You mean clumsy,” she teased, but her heart ached. The warmth of his humor felt like a distant echo of a life they used to share, a life that now felt suspended between the past and an uncertain future.
